pages.title: Why Elci
pages.description: What Elci is, who it is for, how it turns Elm-syntax source into Plutus V3 scripts, and what you get from it today.

pages.title: Installation
pages.description: Build the elci compiler from source with Java 25, optionally as a native executable, and put it on your PATH.

pages.title: Your first validator
pages.description: Create a validator with elci init, read every generated file, check, test and build it, then change it to require a second signature.

pages.title: Anatomy of a project
pages.description: What each file and directory in an Elci project is for, from elci.toml and src/ to tests/ and the build outputs.

pages.title: Build with AI
pages.description: Point Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot or any coding agent at Elci's AI resources, and let it write, check and test Elci contracts.

pages.title: Elci AI starter pack
pages.description: Everything an AI agent needs to write correct Elci on the first try. Ingest this page before generating Elci code.

pages.title: Agent instructions
pages.description: A compact ruleset for AI coding agents working in an Elci project. Save it as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or a Cursor rule.

pages.title: Values, functions and types
pages.description: Elci's basic types, operators, functions with type signatures, lambdas, currying and generic functions, with examples you can run.

pages.title: Conditionals, let and pipelines
pages.description: Make decisions with if and case, name intermediate values with let, chain calls with pipelines, and understand Elci's strict evaluation.

pages.title: Records and tuples
pages.description: Group values with records and tuples, update and destructure them, and see how they are encoded as on-chain data.

pages.title: Custom types and pattern matching
pages.description: Define custom types, match on them exhaustively with case, use Maybe and Result, nest patterns, and see how constructors are encoded on-chain.

pages.title: Lists, dictionaries, maps and arrays
pages.description: Work with Elci's collections, List, Dict, Map and Array, write your own list functions with recursion, and choose the right one for on-chain cost.

pages.title: Modules and imports
pages.description: Split code into modules, control what each module exposes, import Elci modules and Julc Java libraries, and share code between projects.

pages.title: Coming from Elm
pages.description: What carries over from Elm 0.19 to Elci and what changes, from the program model and the core library to Data encoding, Dict, Map and strict decoding.

pages.title: Validators and purposes
pages.description: Declare validators in elci.toml, give each purpose a handler with the right signature, and let one script serve several purposes.

pages.title: Reading the transaction
pages.description: What a handler can read from the ScriptContext, the ledger types behind it, and verified recipes with the Tx and Interval modules for signers, validity ranges, inputs, payments, datums and minting, including the defence against double satisfaction.

pages.title: Datums and redeemers
pages.description: Which types can be datums, redeemers and parameters, how strict decoding protects a validator, the three spending-datum profiles, and exactly how Elci values are encoded as Plutus Data.

pages.title: Parameterized validators
pages.description: Declare deployment parameters, test them with scenarios, and apply them to a built script with elci apply and cardano-cli's detailed Data JSON.

pages.title: Build and deploy
pages.description: What elci build writes, how abi.json and expected-abi guard your data layout, where script hashes come from, and how to load an artifact in Java with Cardano Client Lib.

pages.title: Unit tests
pages.description: Write Bool and Expect tests for your Elci code, run them with elci test, read the results and choose which tests run.

pages.title: Transaction scenarios
pages.description: Test validators with whole transactions. Describe a spend, mint or withdrawal in Elci and elci test runs the deployed script in a complete ledger context.

pages.title: Property-based tests
pages.description: State a rule that must hold for every input, let elci test generate hundreds of inputs, and get the smallest counterexample when the rule breaks.

pages.title: Testing from Java
pages.description: Load the scripts elci build publishes into JUnit, build ledger contexts with julc-testkit and run jqwik property tests with datums generated from the validator's ABI.

pages.title: Debugging and budgets
pages.description: Read elci test failures, find out why a validator rejects a transaction with Debug.trace, and keep execution budgets in check with Scenario.withinBudget.

pages.title: Build a vesting contract
pages.description: Build a vesting validator from an empty directory, with a typed datum and redeemer, a deadline checked against the validity range, a signature check, scenarios and a property test.

pages.title: A treasury and its badge policy
pages.description: Build two cooperating scripts from an empty directory, a treasury that spends payouts and withdraws staking rewards and a badge minting policy, both parameterized by an admin key.

pages.title: A one-shot minting policy
pages.description: Build a minting policy that can mint only once, by tying it to a seed output that the minting transaction must spend, and prove the accept and reject cases with scenarios and properties.

pages.title: Java libraries
pages.description: Import Julc's on-chain Java libraries and your own library JARs into Elci, and learn how Java types, generic methods and imported records map to Elci.

pages.title: Standard library
pages.description: What ships with Elci — Elm's core modules, written in Elci, and Julc's verified Java libraries as gap fillers — how to import them, and the most useful functions of each.

pages.title: Bytes, hashes and bits
pages.description: Build, slice and compare byte strings, convert integers, use bit operations and hashes, verify signatures and print bytes as hex in Elci.

pages.title: Costs and performance
pages.description: Measure execution budgets and script size, understand how strictness and top-level values affect cost, choose between lists, arrays, dictionaries and maps, and know what values cost.

pages.title: How Elci compiles
pages.description: The path from .elm source to a Plutus V3 script — Elci's frontend stages, the boundary with Julc's backend, strict data boundaries and the native executable.

pages.title: CLI
pages.description: Every elci command and option — init, check, build, eval, test, apply and explain — with outputs, exit codes and error formats.

pages.title: elci.toml
pages.description: Every table and key of elci.toml — project settings, validators, entrypoints, Java modules and tests — with the rules the parser enforces and complete examples.

pages.title: Core modules
pages.description: Exact signatures and semantics of Elci's core library, imported by default as in Elm, and of the Dict, Map, Array, Value, Interval, Tx, Bytes, Julc.Data and Debug modules.

pages.title: Test library
pages.description: Complete API of the Expect, Scenario and Property modules that elci test provides to test modules.

pages.title: Language reference
pages.description: Elci's feature matrix, syntax, imports and reserved names, operators and precedence, equality and ordering, constrained type variables, evaluation order and Plutus Data encoding rules.

pages.title: Grammar
pages.description: Elci's formal grammar in EBNF — the lexical grammar, the exact layout rules, the syntactic grammar, operator precedence, the adjacency rules for `.` and `-`, and the Elm syntax Elci rejects.

pages.title: Diagnostics
pages.description: How to read an Elci error, how a run reports several errors, elci explain, the JSON report for tools, and every ELCI error code with real messages and fixes.

pages.title: Example projects
pages.description: The example projects in the Elci repository, what each one demonstrates and how to check, build, test or evaluate it.
